nodes.summary: The conjecture holds: there exist a primitive morphism $\varphi$ on the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ (some power $\varphi^n$ maps every letter to a word containing every letter) and an infinite word $u$ such that $u$ is a fixed point of $\varphi$, $u$ is palindromic (it has arbitrarily long palindromic factors) and uniformly recurrent (for every factor $w$ of $u$ there is $B$ such that, for every $k$, $w$ occurs in $u$…
nodes.title: Labbé's palindromic fixed point outside class P

nodes.summary: The proposition that there exist a primitive morphism $\varphi$ on the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ and an infinite word $u$ such that $u$ is a fixed point of $\varphi$, $u$ is palindromic and uniformly recurrent, and no morphism $\psi$ that has $u$ as a fixed point and is not the identity is conjugate to a morphism in class P.
nodes.title: Palindromic uniformly recurrent fixed point outside class P

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a morphism of the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, acting on finite words letter by letter. Its iterates $\varphi^n$ on finite words are defined by $\varphi^0(w) = w$ and $\varphi^{n+1}(w) = \varphi(\varphi^n(w))$ for every natural number $n$ and every finite word $w$ over $\{0, 1, 2\}$.
nodes.title: Iterated images of words under a morphism

nodes.summary: A morphism $\varphi$ acts on a word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_k$ by $\varphi(w) = \varphi(w_1) \varphi(w_2) \cdots \varphi(w_k)$, the concatenation of the images of its letters; the empty word is sent to the empty word.
nodes.title: Image of a word under a morphism

nodes.summary: A morphism $\varphi$ is in class P (Hof–Knill–Simon) when there is a palindrome $p$ such that for every letter $a$, $\varphi(a) = p q_a$ for some palindrome $q_a$. The palindromes $p$ and $q_a$ may be empty.
nodes.title: Class P

nodes.summary: An infinite word over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is a sequence $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ of letters indexed by the natural numbers, that is, a map $\mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1, 2\}$.
nodes.title: Infinite words

nodes.summary: A finite word $w$ is a factor of an infinite word $u$ when it occurs in $u$ at some position: there is $k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $w_i = u_{k+i}$ for every $i < |w|$ (letters of $w$ indexed from $0$). In particular the empty word is a factor of every infinite word.
nodes.title: Factors of an infinite word

nodes.summary: An infinite word $u$ is a fixed point of a morphism $\varphi$ when it is the limit of the iterates of a prolongable letter: there is a letter $a$ such that $\varphi(a)$ begins with $a$, the words $\varphi^m(a)$ ($m \ge 0$) are arbitrarily long, and every $\varphi^m(a)$ is a prefix of $u$.
nodes.title: Fixed point of a morphism

nodes.summary: A morphism $\psi$ is the identity morphism when $\psi(a)$ is the one-letter word $a$ for every letter $a$.
nodes.title: Identity morphism

nodes.summary: A finite word $w$ over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is a palindrome when it equals its reversal, that is, reads the same backwards; in particular the empty word is a palindrome.
nodes.title: Palindromes

nodes.summary: An infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is palindromic when it has arbitrarily long palindromic factors: for every natural number $N$ there is a finite word $w = w_0 \cdots w_{n-1}$ with $n \ge N$ that reads the same backwards and occurs in $u$: for some position $k$, $w_i = u_{k+i}$ for all $i < n$.
nodes.title: Palindromic infinite words

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a morphism of the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, sending each letter to a finite word, and let $\varphi^n$ be the $n$-th iterate of its letter by letter extension to finite words, with $\varphi^0$ the identity. Then $\varphi$ is primitive when there is a natural number $n$ such that for all letters $a$ and $b$, the letter $b$ occurs in the word $\varphi^n(a)$.
nodes.title: Primitive morphisms

nodes.summary: Let $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ be an infinite word over the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, and say that a finite word $w = w_0 \cdots w_{n-1}$ occurs in $u$ at position $m$ when $w_i = u_{m+i}$ for every $i < n$. Then $u$ is uniformly recurrent when for every finite word $w$ that occurs in $u$ at some position, there is a natural number $B$ such that for every position $k$, the word $w$ occurs in $u$ at position…
nodes.title: Uniformly recurrent infinite words

nodes.summary: Let $\psi$ and $\theta$ be morphisms of the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, each sending every letter to a finite word, and write $xy$ for the concatenation of words $x$ and $y$. Then $\psi$ and $\theta$ are conjugate when there is a finite word $w$ such that $\psi(a) w = w \theta(a)$ for every letter $a$, or there is a finite word $w$ such that $\theta(a) w = w \psi(a)$ for every letter $a$.
nodes.title: Conjugate morphisms

nodes.summary: A morphism of the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is given by its letter map: a function $\varphi$ that sends each letter $a$ to a finite word $\varphi(a)$ over $\{0, 1, 2\}$, possibly the empty word.
nodes.title: Morphisms of the ternary alphabet

nodes.summary: A finite word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{n-1}$ over the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ occurs in an infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over the same alphabet at position $k$ when $w_i = u_{k+i}$ for every $i < n$.
nodes.title: Occurrence of a word at a position

nodes.summary: The alphabet is the three-letter set $\{0, 1, 2\}$.
nodes.title: The ternary alphabet of Labbé's counterexample

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
